theorems.name: Submission.p06_9e0f5043ff_fpm_rd_eval_kernel
theorems.statement: ∀ (K F : Type*) [Field K] [Field F] [Algebra K F] (x : F), Transcendental K x → ∀ q : Polynomial K, Irreducible q → ∀ v : AlgebraicCurve.Place K F, (∀ f : F, f ∈ v.toValuationSubring ↔ ∃ a b : Polynomial K, ¬ q ∣ b ∧ f = Polynomial.aeval x a / Polynomial.aeval x b) → ∃ e : Polynomial K →ₐ[K] v.toValuationSubring, (∀ a : Polynomial K, (e a : F) = Polynomial.aeval x a) ∧ RingHom.ker ((IsLocalRing.residue v.toValuationSubring).comp e.toRingHom) = Ideal.span ({q} : Set (Polynomial K))
theorems.natural_summary: Denominator 1 lifts evaluation into the valuation ring. Transcendence makes evaluation injective, and permitted inverse fractions make e(a) a unit whenever q does not divide a. An inverse for e(q), expressed as an allowed fraction, would imply b = q*a, contradicting the denominator condition. Thus e(q) has zero residue, while evaluations of polynomials not divisible by q have nonzero residue. Kernel membership therefore coincides exactly with divisibility by q.
